story: E005-F009-S002: Implement advanced hook builder view with canvas visualization
story_description: As a power user managing complex hook workflows, I need a visual canvas-based builder that displays hook chains as connected nodes, allowing me to understand the flow of events through triggers, actions, and conditions at a glance, and edit hook configurations through an intuitive node inspector panel.
task: E005-F009-S002-T001: Create AdvancedHookBuilderView with provider selector and canvas controls
task_description: Implement the AdvancedHookBuilderView SwiftUI view that provides a visual hook workflow builder with three-pane layout: node palette on left, interactive canvas in center, and hook inspector panel on right. Include provider selector dropdown (Claude Code, Gemini, Codex disabled), zoom controls with keyboard shortcuts, Test and Export buttons in toolbar, and variable reference panel showing available hook environment variables.
atom_description: Create the AdvancedHookBuilderView.swift file in Blaze/Sources/Settings/Hooks/ that implements the visual hook builder interface. The view uses a three-pane NavigationSplitView layout with: (1) left sidebar containing categorized node palette for event triggers, actions, and conditions, (2) center canvas with pan/zoom gestures rendering hook nodes as cards connected by bezier curves, and (3) right inspector panel showing editable properties for the selected node including name, event type, matcher regex, hook type radio buttons, timeout field, and prompt/command text editor with variable interpolation hints.
problem_statement: The current HooksBuilderView provides basic functionality for creating and editing hooks, but power users need a more sophisticated visual interface that shows hook workflows as connected node graphs. Without this visualization: (1) users cannot easily understand complex multi-step hook chains, (2) users cannot see the flow from event triggers through conditions to actions, (3) users cannot visually identify gaps or misconnections in their hook logic, and (4) users cannot reference available environment variables when writing hook prompts or commands. The AdvancedHookBuilderView addresses these gaps by providing a canvas-based node editor with comprehensive inspector panel.

edge_cases: Edge case 1: Empty pipeline with no nodes - Canvas shows empty state, Test/Export buttons disabled
Edge case 2: Single node with no connections - Valid minimal pipeline, can be exported
Edge case 3: Disconnected nodes - Validation warning but not blocking
Edge case 4: Circular connections - Validation error preventing export
Edge case 5: Very long command string - Text editor scrolls, node card truncates
Edge case 6: Zoom at minimum scale 0.25 - Zoom out button disabled
Edge case 7: Zoom at maximum scale 4.0 - Zoom in button disabled
Edge case 8: Node dragged off-screen - Canvas pan allows retrieving node
Edge case 9: Rapid zoom gestures - Debounce to prevent jank
Edge case 10: Test command hangs - 30 second timeout with error message
Edge case 11: Provider changed during edit - Warn if hooks incompatible
Edge case 12: Network error loading hooks - Show error message with retry option
Edge case 13: Concurrent edits to same hook - Last write wins, no conflict resolution
Edge case 14: Special characters in command - Properly escaped for bash execution
Edge case 15: Delete last node in pipeline - Returns to empty state
failure_modes: FM-001: HooksInstallationService.listInstalledHooks throws - Catch error, log message, show empty state with error banner - Low severity, recoverable
FM-002: HooksInstallationService.installHooks throws - Catch error, show alert with error details, keep user in editor - Medium severity, recoverable
FM-003: runTestCommand process fails to start - Catch error, record failure in test results - Low severity, informational
FM-004: runTestCommand times out after 30s - Terminate process, record timeout in test results - Low severity, informational
FM-005: Pipeline validation returns errors - Block export, show errors in test results sheet - Low severity, expected behavior
FM-006: InstalledHookSummary.toPipeline() throws - Catch error, log message, show error alert - Medium severity, recoverable
FM-007: Canvas gesture recognizer conflicts - Use simultaneousGesture modifier to avoid blocking - Low severity, UX issue
FM-008: Memory pressure with many nodes - Implement lazy node rendering if needed - Medium severity, performance

risks: Risk 1: Canvas gesture conflicts between pan, zoom, and node drag cause UX issues
Risk 2: Performance degradation with 50+ nodes due to view recomputation
Risk 3: Test command execution blocks main thread causing UI freeze
Risk 4: Memory leak from retained closures in canvas gesture handlers
Risk 5: Provider selection state lost when navigating away and back
mitigations: Mitigation 1: Use simultaneousGesture and gesture priority modifiers to resolve conflicts
Mitigation 2: Implement lazy rendering for off-screen nodes using GeometryReader
Mitigation 3: Execute commands in Task on background thread with @MainActor UI updates
Mitigation 4: Use weak self capture in closures and verify with Instruments
Mitigation 5: Persist selectedProvider in UserDefaults or SettingsStore
risk_register.blast_radius: Medium - This is a new view file that does not modify existing functionality. Failure would prevent visual hook editing but list-based editing and manual settings.json editing remain available as fallbacks.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If implementation blocked, users can continue using the existing HooksBuilderView which has canvas functionality already. The AdvancedHookBuilderView provider selector and variable reference enhancements can be added incrementally.
